🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 8)
Channel: alert-frontend... no — *alert-system*  •  bug-type guess: unknown (likely code/data — transient exception on REST tables-read path)  •  alerts in group: 3
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Vertical App Experience` (`@sales management` / `#team-sales-management`)

Symptoms:
  - Monitor 70171778 "Unexpected number of 5XX errors" tripped 11:17–11:24Z, self-recovered (OK 11:24:38Z).
  - **90 × HTTP 500** on `rest-api` (runtime-core public REST host), all on one endpoint: `GET /api/v{version}/tables/{table}`. Error rate ≈ 0.51% of 17,818 hits; peak rolling-5min ≈ 82 vs threshold 30.
  - ⚠️ *2nd identical occurrence* — 2026-06-16 (`cb96c9950d20bb7d`) was 75×500 on the SAME endpoint, same monitor, same self-recovery.

Trace IDs: n/a — these 500s are APM-only (not in Serilog); see DD APM traces link below.
Likely cause: transient SQL/app exception on the per-tenant table-read path; brief and self-recovered. Exact exception *undetermined* — not written to Serilog/ES (ES is back up, 17-day 401 resolved, but this signature is APM-only) and traces carry no `@account_name`.
Suggested next action: **file a defect** against the runtime-core REST `GET tables/{table}` handler (the 06-16 follow-up said "if it recurs, file a defect" — it has). Recommend adding a Serilog Error write (account + exception) on that catch path so the next occurrence is diagnosable + auto-classifiable. Consider seeding a recurrence-tracking KI (proposed in the investigation report).

Source alerts (3 total):
  • https://methodme.slack.com/archives/CPHHABKAA/p1781781463355899  (alert-system, 11:17 UTC)
  • https://methodme.slack.com/archives/CPHHABKAA/p1781781821969569  (alert-system, 11:23 UTC)

  • DD APM traces: https://app.datadoghq.com/apm/traces?query=env%3Aprod%20service%3Arest-api%20http.status_code%3A5*&start=1781780700000&end=1781782200000
  • DD metric (5XX by service): https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&exp_metric=trace.aspnet_core.request.errors&exp_scope=env%3Aprod%2Chttp.status_code%3A5*&exp_agg=sum&start=1781780700&end=1781782200

  • Investigation: docs/investigations/2026-06-18-93f48e606430b954.md

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-05-24-runtime-core-rtc-p95-recurring` (ki-24)
Occurrence #~48 in the last 7 days (total occ now 180). Latency-only RTC contention — DM'd because last notification was 2026-06-17 11:08Z (~26h ago, past the 24h suppression window).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Vertical App Experience` (`@sales management` / `#team-sales-management`)
Playbook: confirm latency-only (runtime-core status:error = 0), then pull DD APM @duration:>5s outlier traces in the spike window to identify the slow span (SQL/Mongo/Redis) by @account_name/tenant — still the open diagnostic gap. fix_status: investigating · no Jira.

This cycle = one sustained runtime-core RTC contention window 12:10–13:07Z, surfaced across two channels (two root-cause groups, same event):
• Group A 4b89c1297bcf47bf — alert-runtime-monitoring 12:25:05Z (MAX-forwarder bot B063S8NBW0M)
• Group B d92209ce75a769d5 — alert-system Redis Errors monitor 12:52:38Z + 12:58:36Z (suppressed → actionable.md; same KB)

Symptoms / evidence: RTC Screen Load p95 max 2.66s + Action Exec p95 max 2.74s BOTH <3s (alert-system p95 monitors did NOT trip; only MAX-forwarder fired); RTC MAX pervasive (Action Exec 44.15s@12:43, 39.94s@12:50; Screen Load 24.23s@12:59, 26.25s@13:04); Redis cmd-errors 96 on nonprod/apps @12:51 (baseline 0) concurrent with RTC MAX burst = RTC/Redis backpressure; latency-only confirmed (0 runtime-core errors, 5XX all <=2/5min vs 30, no cascade); no deploy (43d), no ki-21 co-fire, no swat.

Source alerts (3 total): runtime-monitoring 12:25 + alert-system 12:52 & 12:58 (permalinks). Evidence: DD monitors 115456700/117279738/227940275 + DD logs + Kibana. Suggested next action: monitor — known latency-only pattern, no cascade, self-recovered.
